review_comments.body:
```suggestion
```

or is any of those causing the build to fail?
Why do we not make this part of the main package, possible as an extra output?
It would be better to patch the cmake files so we know when we can remove this again.

that would entail patching the cmake files *inside* the vendored crate sources, which seems a lot more brittle and unnecessary effort compared to just checking if the build fails with these flags removed

i decided against having it as an extra output on the main package but decided against that to make it easier to find for end-users as one needs it to generate the mandatory key. (also this is just the install phase for this python script, and i didn't know a better way of packaging a random script, though i am not well versed in the nixpkgs python ecosystem)

```
       >
       > error[E0277]: the trait bound `AppState: Default` is not satisfied
       >    --> autoconnect/autoconnect-ws/autoconnect-ws-sm/src/unidentified.rs:295:15
       >     |
       > 295 |             ..Default::default()
       >     |               ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ the trait `Default` is not implemented for `AppState`
```
i am not even sure if the unit tests are still maintained by upstream or if they fully rely on their docker stack for end to end testing
mainly because all other modular services don't use it either (one of reasons for that is probably that one doesn't have access to the `finalPackage` from inside the module, but thats just my guess)
actually yeah no reason to not use it since pkgs is passed into it anyways
sleeping over it: having it as a special output is the right call as the script will only ever be used once and the modular service can just depend on the main `out` output

shouldn't package be under  `autoendpoint`?

```suggestion
    autoendpoint = {
        package = lib.mkPackageOption pkgs "autopush-rs.out" { };
```

otherwise, https://search.nixos.org doesn't have the best UX

see https://search.nixos.org/options?channel=unstable&query=auto&source=modular_service
`package` is listed without reference to which service unless you click and read which module is from, also clicking to see details opens the 2 `package` entry since they collide
hmm, imo it is more convenient to have it in the service toplevel, but i don't have strong opinions on it (especially as one should rarely need to change the default). feel free to open a PR
It's mostly about collisions on the nixos search webpage
generally i think that's something the web-search should work on (ie add some identifier)
